messages:
sara: Heads-up - seeing a sharp p95/p99 latency spike from eu-west POP starting ~12:15 UTC. P95 went from ~90ms -> ~1.2s, throughput dipped ~18%. No obvious error rate increase.
raj: Noted. Any recent deployments or config rollouts to runtime in that window?
maria: We pushed a kernel-selection tweak (auto-fallback heuristics) at 12:05 UTC to prefer FP16 optimized kernels on older GPUs. Roll ID: r-2026-03-18-0912.
sara: That matches timing. Also saw KV cache hit ratio drop ~15% around same time in dashboards. Could be related.
perf-bot: Perf alert: eu-west tail latency regression detected. Probe run summary attached.
tomasz: Pulling profiling traces now. If kernel fallback chooses slower kernels, it could increase CPU scheduling and thrash KV cache due to longer request time.
maria: Confirming: fallback path adds a ~200ms per-request compute delta in our microbenchmarks on a 16k context.
raj: Can you dump a quick sample of request traces with kernel labels? javatrace or runtime logs?
tomasz: Pasting a few lines from runtime logs (filtered):
```
[12:17:02] request_id=ZQf3 kernel=fp16-opt fallback=true exec_ms=198 queue_ms=12 kv_hit=false
[12:17:05] request_id=Ah9b kernel=fp32 exec_ms=45 queue_ms=8 kv_hit=true
[12:17:07] request_id=Kp2m kernel=fp16-opt fallback=true exec_ms=210 queue_ms=15 kv_hit=false
```
raj: Interesting - fallback=true with kv_hit=false correlation. That suggests longer execution windows causing KV entries to be evicted or missed.
sara: Also saw host-level CPU steal on some hosts (provider reported noisy neighbor). dstat snapshot: cpu%user high, cpu%stolen spikes aligned to latency window.
maria: Could be twofold: provider-side noisy neighbor + our kernel fallback increasing residency time (worse for eviction-sensitive caches).
perf-bot: KV cache eviction counter spiked +43% at 12:16:30 in eu-west pool-a.
raj: If it's noisy neighbor we should confirm network path/DNS changes too. Any signs of cross-region routing? traceroute/TC output?
tomasz: Doing tcptraceroute to model servers from affected POP: shows an extra hop through ams-2 (net hop 7) for ~30% of flows during spike window, adding ~80ms.
sara: So some requests got routed via another region which + fallback kernel = compounded tail.
maria: I want to check recent infra control plane changes: nothing changed in routing but we did flip a provider peering to reduce costs earlier today, rolled at 11:50 UTC.
raj: That peering flip could explain extra AS hops and noisy neighbor if traffic moved to different hosts.
omasz: (typo) - tomasz: Also correlating attach logs show a specific host (eu-west-host-27) had persistent swap pressure and high interrupt rates. That host ran several non-dedicated tenants.
sara: Action proposals: 1) revert kernel-selection tweak (quick rollback) 2) evacuate/cordon eu-west-host-27 and drain 3) temporarily disable auto-fallback to FP16 on this pool 4) open ticket with provider about peering+steal.
maria: I can roll back the kernel-selection tweak now (will take ~6 mins to roll). Rolling back to r-2026-03-18-0818.
raj: I'll prepare a cordon+drain plan for host-27 and spin up replacement capacity in eu-west-standby.
tomasz: I'll throttle batch sizes on the affected pool to reduce request residency and reduce KV eviction pressure (reduce max_batch from 64 -> 24).
perf-bot: Patch: batch size change applied to pool eu-west-a (max_batch=24).
infra-bot: Cordoning eu-west-host-27 now. Drain tasks -> 10 -> 3 -> 0 (drain complete).
sara: Rollback started by maria. Monitoring metrics.
maria: Rollback complete at 12:28 UTC. Kernel labels now show preferred kernels without fallback.
perf-bot: Observed p95 trending down: 1.2s -> 260ms within 4m. KV hit ratio recovering. Throughput back to -3% vs baseline.
omasz: tomasz: After drain, steal metrics dropped on that host group.
raj: Provider ticket opened (PR-7291) referencing peering flip and transient routing: sent traceroutes and BGP paths.
sara: Good work. Immediate mitigation summary: rolled back kernel fallback, drained noisy host, reduced batch size, opened provider ticket.
maria: Postmortem items: - add canary to kernel-selection change with traffic caps - add KV cache eviction alerting with causal link to exec_ms - add provider routing verification to deploy checklist - consider tenant isolation for noisy workloads in eu-west.
tomasz: I'll attach the perf traces and flamegraphs to the ticket.
raj: Assign owners: maria (rollback/process), tomasz (profiling artifacts), raj (infrastructure/drain+provider), sara (postmortem writeup).
sara: ETA on final postmortem by EOD tomorrow. Anyone else spotting lingering issues?
perf-bot: Follow-up metric: p99 back to baseline after 10m.
maria: I'll keep an eye on any regressions and disable auto-fallback rollout until we add stronger guards. :thumbsup:
sara: Thanks all — closing incident thread, will create the formal incident doc with links to traces and provider replies.
raj: thx, nice triage.
